newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar, sterling energized by brief nap.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar, sterling energized by brief nap.

text.p: The dollar stands ready for another charge at the February 1994 high of 1.7686 marks in coming sessions after a mild pullback rekindled buying interest, technical analysts said on Thursday.
The dollar/mark dip stopped short of important supports below 1.7450 and appears to have been a side effect of a decline in sterling/mark and a rebound in mark/yen.

"Retracements of one or two pfennigs have been typical in this dollar/mark move higher. We're taking a breather at a critical resistance and then going much higher," said Keith Raphael, president of Crosscurrents Investment Advisory.

However, Elliot Wave analysis shows dollar/mark's rally terminating after a push toward 1.78 marks in the weeks ahead. The current fourth-wave should end near 1.7425, yielding a fifth wave, which would typically lack momentum, said Elliott Wave International currency research director Jim Chorek.
"The bull market is getting tired, even though we expect one more new high," said Chorek. "We could get a real sharp selloff once we get near 1.78."
Sterling/mark remains comfortably above major support below 2.9350, which represents a congestion zone or a previous Elliott Wave fourth-wave support, chartists said.
"Sterling/mark is very stable above 2.9350 and it's showing resilience after completing a correction," said Raphael. "My long-term objective is 2.9940 and we could be getting there a little early."
Dollar/yen sits within an apparent triangle, but should fight its way toward 115 in coming sessions, analysts said.
Key support sits at 111.80, a 76.4-percent retrace of a two-day run from 110.62 to 115.70 on June 11-12, Chorek said.
"We're moving into a slightly bullish stance as long as 111.80 holds," Chorek said. "That rally was impulsive, meaning the trend is up."
Mark/yen may have bottomed after holding above key support near 63.40, technicians said.
That level represents at 61.8-percent retracement of the impulsive 1995 rally from 57.28 to 73.41, and its preservation during the recent mark/yen dip exudes bullishness, Chorek said.
"I suspect we are probably in a change of trend here. We could get a turnaround rally and break above 67.25, which is a previous fourth-wave resistance," he added.
